definitions.explanation: Having printed horizontal lines on the page, as in a lined notebook or ruled paper. A common product descriptor for stationery.

examples.japanese: {罫線入|けいせんい}りのノートを{買|か}った。
{罫線入|けいせんい}りの{便箋|びんせん}のほうが、きれいに{書|か}ける。
examples.english: Lined writing paper makes it easier to write neatly.

examples.japanese: この{手帳|てちょう}は{罫線入|けいせんい}りのページと{無地|むじ}のページが{交互|こうご}になっている。
examples.english: This planner alternates between lined pages and blank pages.

notes:
Composed of {罫線|けいせん} (ruled line) and {入|い}り (containing/with). The suffix 〜{入|い}り is productive and means "containing" or "with," as in {砂糖入|さとうい}り (with sugar) or {絵入|えい}り (illustrated).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {罫線入|けいせんい}りのノート: lined notebook
- {罫線入|けいせんい}りの{用紙|ようし}: ruled paper
- {罫線入|けいせんい}りの{便箋|びんせん}: lined writing paper

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {横罫|よこけい}: horizontal ruling — specifies horizontal lines
- {方眼|ほうがん}: grid/graph — square grid pattern
- {無地|むじ}: plain/blank — no lines
- {罫線|けいせん}: ruled line — the base word
